Gonococcal disease produces migratory tenosynovitis with pustular skin lesions over days to a fortnight, not eight weeks of persistent swelling with nail changes (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

explanation.summary: Growth hormone excess in adults advances slowly enough that neither the patient nor the family notices, so the diagnosis is typically made about a decade after onset and is often prompted by comparing old photographs. Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnoea, carpal tunnel syndrome and arthropathy are the systemic consequences that bring the patient to medical attention. Screening is biochemical and localisation follows, because pituitary incidentalomas are common enough that imaging first generates confusion. Most cases arise from a somatotroph macroadenoma, so visual fields and anterior pituitary function are assessed once the diagnosis is biochemically established. Untreated disease roughly doubles mortality, driven by cardiovascular disease, and there is an increased incidence of colorectal neoplasia that shapes surveillance.
key_points: Insulin like growth factor 1 against an age matched range is the screening test.
Random growth hormone is uninterpretable because secretion is pulsatile.
Failure to suppress growth hormone after an oral glucose load is confirmatory when screening is equivocal.
Image the pituitary only after biochemical confirmation, given the frequency of incidentalomas.
Hypertension, diabetes, sleep apnoea and arthropathy drive the excess mortality.
explanation.pearls: Old photographs spanning ten to fifteen years are a genuine diagnostic instrument here: soft tissue change of this speed is invisible to daily observers, and the photographic comparison often precedes the biochemistry by a single consultation.

sources.label: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Acromegaly

options.rationale: Growth hormone is secreted in pulses with troughs that reach the undetectable range in healthy people, so a single value neither confirms nor excludes excess (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology).

Failure of growth hormone to suppress after a glucose load remains the confirmatory test, but it is used to resolve an equivocal or discordant screening result rather than as the first step (Source: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Acromegaly).
source_refs: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Acromegaly

options.rationale: Imaging localises a lesion once biochemical excess is proven, and performing it first risks acting on an incidental pituitary lesion found in about a tenth of adults (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology).

This peptide has a half life of many hours and reflects integrated growth hormone secretion across the day, so a single sample compared with an age matched range is the recommended screening test (Source: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Acromegaly).
source_refs: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Acromegaly

options.rationale: Cortisol excess would explain hypertension and glucose intolerance but not acral enlargement, interdental spacing or macroglossia, and there are no striae or proximal weakness (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology).

explanation.summary: Hereditary haemochromatosis is the commonest inherited disorder in Australians of northern European ancestry, and the great majority of clinically affected people are homozygous for the C282Y variant of the HFE gene. Transferrin saturation rises before ferritin and is the more specific screening measure, since ferritin alone rises with alcohol, obesity, metabolic dysfunction associated fatty liver and any inflammatory state. The second and third metacarpophalangeal joints are the classical arthropathy and often the earliest symptom, preceding diabetes, cardiomyopathy, hypogonadism and cirrhosis. Treatment is weekly venesection to a ferritin target of 50 to 100 mcg/L followed by lifelong maintenance every three to four months. Confirming the genotype matters beyond the individual, because first degree relatives can then be offered testing before organ damage occurs.
key_points: Transferrin saturation above 45 per cent with raised ferritin triggers HFE genotyping.
Ferritin alone is an acute phase reactant and rises with alcohol, obesity and inflammation.
Second and third metacarpophalangeal arthropathy is often the earliest clinical feature.
Genotype first so that cascade testing of first degree relatives has a defined target.
Liver biopsy now stages fibrosis in high ferritin disease rather than making the diagnosis.
explanation.pearls: Ferritin above 1000 mcg/L with a raised alanine aminotransferase identifies the subgroup at real risk of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, and this is the threshold at which fibrosis staging is added rather than proceeding straight to venesection alone.

options.rationale: Biopsy has been displaced from the diagnostic pathway by genetic testing and now serves mainly to stage fibrosis when ferritin exceeds 1000 mcg/L, so it follows rather than precedes the genotype (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia: Haemochromatosis).

Magnetic resonance quantification is a non-invasive alternative for measuring hepatic iron and monitoring response, but it does not identify the inherited defect that determines family testing (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia: Haemochromatosis).

Repeating is the right move when ferritin is raised with a normal saturation, since ferritin behaves as an acute phase reactant, but a saturation of 71 per cent with a C reactive protein of 3 mg/L already excludes that explanation (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia: Haemochromatosis).

Venesection is the correct treatment but starting it before genotyping removes the chance to confirm the diagnosis and denies his siblings and children a clear basis for cascade testing (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia: Haemochromatosis).

A transferrin saturation above 45 per cent with a raised ferritin in a man with a suggestive family history is the trigger for genotyping, and confirming C282Y homozygosity establishes the diagnosis and enables cascade screening of relatives (Source: Gastroenterological Society of Australia: Haemochromatosis).

explanation.summary: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy in a young adult has a short differential dominated by sarcoidosis, lymphoma and tuberculosis, and the accompanying features usually settle it without histology. The acute syndrome of erythema nodosum, symmetrical hilar nodes, ankle arthritis and fever carries a distinctly good prognosis, with spontaneous resolution in most patients within one to two years. Deciding not to biopsy is an active clinical judgement that requires the picture to be typical and the alternatives to be improbable, which is why the negative interferon gamma release assay and the absence of constitutional weight loss matter. Baseline assessment still includes spirometry with diffusing capacity, corrected calcium, renal and liver function, an electrocardiogram and ophthalmology review, since asymptomatic cardiac and eye involvement changes management. Corticosteroid is withheld unless a threatened organ is identified, because it does not alter the natural history of the acute syndrome.
key_points: Erythema nodosum plus symmetrical hilar nodes plus ankle arthritis and fever is a specific acute syndrome that usually remits.
Biopsy is reserved for an atypical, asymmetric or constitutionally suspicious picture.
Corticosteroid indications are declining lung function, hypercalcaemia, and cardiac, neurological or ocular disease.
Baseline workup includes lung function, calcium, electrocardiogram and ophthalmology review.
Asymmetric or necrotic nodes with a positive interferon gamma release assay point instead to tuberculosis.
explanation.pearls: Cardiac involvement is present in about a quarter of patients at autopsy but symptomatic in far fewer, so an electrocardiogram at diagnosis is the cheap screen that catches conduction block before it presents as syncope or sudden death.

options.rationale: The triad of erythema nodosum, symmetrical hilar lymphadenopathy and ankle arthritis with fever is a recognised acute presentation that remits spontaneously in the large majority within two years, so anti inflammatory treatment with interval imaging is sufficient (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory).

Tissue sampling is required when the picture is atypical, asymmetric or suggests lymphoma, but this constellation is specific enough that biopsy is not needed and adds procedural risk (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory).

Systemic corticosteroid is reserved for progressive lung function decline, hypercalcaemia, or cardiac, neurological or ocular involvement, and normal spirometry with normal calcium removes each of those indications (Source: BMJ Best Practice: Sarcoidosis).

Tuberculous adenopathy is characteristically asymmetric and often necrotic, and the negative interferon gamma release assay with no exposure history makes it improbable (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Steroid sparing immunosuppression belongs to chronic disease that has failed or become dependent on corticosteroid, and committing to it at first presentation of a self-limiting syndrome is disproportionate (Source: BMJ Best Practice: Sarcoidosis).

explanation.summary: Opioid neurotoxicity is a syndrome of delirium, myoclonus, hyperalgesia and allodynia that develops when active metabolites accumulate faster than they are cleared, most often because renal function has quietly deteriorated rather than because the dose has changed. Morphine is the highest risk agent in Australian practice because both its analgesic and its neuroexcitatory metabolites depend on renal clearance, whereas fentanyl and methadone are metabolised to inactive products. Rotation is done at a reduced equianalgesic dose, typically 25 to 50 per cent lower, because cross tolerance between opioids is incomplete and the previous dose was already producing toxicity. Rehydration alone will often improve matters and should accompany the switch. The commonest missed contributors are dehydration from vomiting, a recently added non-steroidal anti inflammatory, and hypercalcaemia, so each is checked at the same time.
key_points: Delirium with myoclonus and hyperalgesia on an unchanged opioid dose points to metabolite accumulation.
Falling renal function is the usual trigger, so check creatinine before adjusting analgesia.
Rotate at 25 to 50 per cent below the calculated equianalgesic dose because cross tolerance is incomplete.
Fentanyl and methadone lack renally cleared active metabolites and are preferred in renal impairment.
Naloxone is for respiratory depression, not for neurotoxic delirium with a normal respiratory rate.
explanation.pearls: Morphine 3 glucuronide has no analgesic activity at all but is neuroexcitatory, which is why the patient becomes more agitated and more pain sensitive as the dose rises, the opposite of what escalation is meant to achieve.

options.rationale: Reading agitation as uncontrolled pain and escalating the same opioid is the classic error, because more morphine means more accumulated metabolite and deeper neurotoxicity (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Palliative Care).

A benzodiazepine can suppress the myoclonus as a short term adjunct but leaves the accumulating metabolite in place and adds sedation that worsens the delirium (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Palliative Care).

Reversal is for life threatening respiratory depression, which a rate of 16 breaths per minute with normal pupils excludes, and it would strip away analgesia and precipitate a pain crisis (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Myoclonus, hallucinations and hyperalgesia on a stable dose as renal function falls indicate accumulation of morphine 6 and morphine 3 glucuronide, and switching to an opioid without renally cleared active metabolites while rehydrating reverses it (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Palliative Care).
Hypercalcaemia is the alternative cause of delirium worth excluding in metastatic disease, but a corrected calcium of 2.42 mmol/L takes it off the table (Source: eviQ: Hypercalcaemia of malignancy).

explanation.summary: Cobalamin deficiency produces a megaloblastic anaemia and a distinct neurological syndrome affecting the dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts, which is why absent ankle jerks coexist with upgoing plantar responses. The neurological disease can appear with a normal haemoglobin and a normal mean cell volume, particularly when concurrent iron deficiency or thalassaemia trait masks the macrocytosis, so normal indices never exclude it. Autoimmune gastritis with loss of intrinsic factor is the commonest cause in an Australian adult with another autoimmune disease, and it clusters with autoimmune thyroid disease and type 1 diabetes. Recovery of the anaemia is reliable but neurological recovery depends on duration, with damage present for more than six to twelve months often only partially reversible. Patients with autoimmune gastritis carry an increased risk of gastric neuroendocrine tumours and adenocarcinoma, so persistent symptoms warrant endoscopy.
key_points: Replace cobalamin before folate; folate alone can precipitate subacute combined degeneration.
Absent ankle jerks with upgoing plantars is the signature of combined dorsal column and corticospinal disease.
Neurological deficiency can occur with a normal haemoglobin and a normal mean cell volume.
Parenteral loading is preferred when neurological signs are present.
Autoimmune gastritis clusters with thyroid disease and raises long term gastric cancer risk.
explanation.pearls: Watch the potassium in the first week of replacement: brisk erythropoiesis after loading can drop serum potassium sharply, and a repeat electrolyte panel at day three to five is standard when the initial anaemia is severe.

sources.label: National Blood Authority: Patient Blood Management Guidelines
BMJ Best Practice: Vitamin B12 deficiency

options.rationale: Replacing folate while cobalamin is deficient can correct the anaemia while the spinal cord disease accelerates, and this precipitation of subacute combined degeneration is the specific harm the sequence is designed to prevent (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Transfusion treats the number rather than the deficiency, and in a slowly developed macrocytic anaemia with a compensated circulation it carries fluid overload risk without addressing the neurology (Source: National Blood Authority: Patient Blood Management Guidelines).
source_refs: National Blood Authority: Patient Blood Management Guidelines

options.rationale: Cobalamin is replaced first and folate added afterwards, and parenteral loading is used when neurological signs are present because the priority is halting cord and peripheral nerve damage before it becomes irreversible (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

High dose oral replacement works through passive absorption and suits uncomplicated deficiency, but parenteral loading is preferred where cord signs demand rapid and certain repletion (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

The antibody result establishes the mechanism and shapes lifelong follow up including gastric cancer awareness, but treatment is not held pending a test that takes days while myelin is being lost (Source: BMJ Best Practice: Vitamin B12 deficiency).
source_refs: BMJ Best Practice: Vitamin B12 deficiency

explanation.summary: Medication overuse headache develops in people with an underlying primary headache disorder who take acute treatments too frequently, and it is one of the commonest reasons a previously episodic migraine becomes daily. Opioid and combination analgesics carry the highest risk and convert at around 10 days of use per month, while simple analgesics require about 15 days. Management is withdrawal of the overused agent, an explanation that headache will transiently worsen for one to two weeks, and simultaneous introduction of a preventive so the patient is not left without any plan. Most patients revert to their original episodic pattern within two months of withdrawal, which is also the diagnostic confirmation. Persistent daily headache beyond that point should prompt review for a second diagnosis.
key_points: Headache on 15 or more days per month plus acute medication overuse for more than three months in a known headache sufferer defines the syndrome
Opioid and combination analgesics trigger it at 10 or more days per month, simple analgesics at 15 or more
Withdrawal of the overused drug is the treatment, not addition of a second acute agent
Start a preventive at the time of withdrawal to cover the rebound period
Imaging is reserved for red flags, which are absent when the examination and fundoscopy are normal
explanation.pearls: Warn the patient that withdrawal headache peaks in the first three to seven days and settles within two weeks, because patients who are not warned almost always resume the tablets on about day four.

sources.label: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition

options.rationale: Adding a second acute agent to near daily analgesic use sustains the overuse pattern, and triptans themselves cause this syndrome at ten or more days per month. It would be reasonable only once acute use is back under about two days per week (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

Imaging is indicated for red flags such as thunderclap onset, papilloedema, new deficit, immunosuppression or new headache after age 50, none of which she has. Delaying withdrawal while awaiting a scan prolongs the very exposure that is driving the pain (Source: RACGP: Headache in general practice).

Headache on 15 or more days a month with acute medication on 15 or more days for over three months in a known migraineur is medication overuse headache, and withdrawal of the offending drug is the treatment. Starting a preventive at the same time reduces the withdrawal headache and improves the chance of reverting to episodic migraine (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).
source_refs: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition

options.rationale: Preventive medication started while the overused analgesic continues has a much lower response rate, because ongoing exposure maintains central sensitisation. Amitriptyline is a reasonable preventive choice but only alongside withdrawal (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

Nerve blocks are an adjunct used in specialist practice for refractory headache and do not address the daily codeine exposure that is generating the pattern. Referral first also delays the intervention with the largest effect (Source: RACGP: Headache in general practice).

explanation.summary: Recurrent lower limb cellulitis is driven by a portal of entry, most often interdigital tinea or a fissure, acting on a limb with impaired lymphatic drainage, and each episode causes further lymphatic damage that raises the risk of the next. The prophylaxis evidence shows a clear reduction in recurrence while penicillin is being taken, with the benefit fading once it stops, so the decision is one of ongoing risk rather than a fixed course. Prophylaxis is offered when there have been two or more episodes in a year and a predisposing factor persists. It never replaces the other two limbs of management, which are eradicating the portal of entry and maintaining compression. Patients allergic to penicillin can use a macrolide for the same indication.
key_points: Two or more episodes in a year plus a persisting predisposing factor is the threshold for prophylaxis
Interdigital tinea is the commonest portal of entry and must be treated to make prophylaxis effective
Benefit is present while the antibiotic is taken and wanes after cessation, so review is scheduled rather than a stop date assumed
Compression therapy reduces limb volume and further episodes and belongs in the same plan
Absent erythema, normal C reactive protein and normal white cell count confirm this is prevention, not treatment of active infection
explanation.pearls: Look between the toes at every cellulitis review, because untreated tinea pedis is the single most modifiable portal of entry and topical terbinafine for two to four weeks clears most cases.

sources.label: PATCH I trial, New England Journal of Medicine

options.rationale: Intermittent dosing given only around relapses does not maintain the continuous exposure that the prophylaxis evidence rests on, and this agent is used this way for streptococcal rheumatic fever prophylaxis rather than for cellulitis. Continuous oral therapy is the studied regimen here (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Two or more episodes of cellulitis in a year with a persistent predisposing factor such as lymphoedema is the trigger for long term antistreptococcal prophylaxis, which roughly halves recurrence while it is being taken. Treating the interdigital tinea and reinstating compression are essential adjuncts rather than alternatives (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).
source_refs: PATCH I trial, New England Journal of Medicine

options.rationale: Clearing the web space removes an important portal of entry and must be done, but on its own it leaves the lymphoedema and the established recurrence pattern untreated. It would be sufficient only if this were a first episode without lymphoedema (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

Compression reduces limb volume and is part of the plan, but it does not by itself provide the antistreptococcal cover that recurrent disease with four episodes in a year warrants. Compression alone is appropriate where episodes are infrequent (Source: Australasian Lymphology Association: Position statement).

Pulsed broad spectrum therapy has no evidence base in this setting and selects resistance while leaving unprotected intervals. Doxycycline is reserved for suspected non multiresistant Staphylococcus aureus disease rather than routine streptococcal prophylaxis (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

explanation.summary: The National Bowel Cancer Screening Program mails immunochemical faecal occult blood test kits to Australians in the eligible age range, and the entire benefit of the program depends on positive results proceeding to colonoscopy. Participation is good but follow up colonoscopy rates are not, and the largest avoidable harm in the pathway is a positive result attributed to haemorrhoids or a normal blood count. A normal haemoglobin and ferritin do not reduce the probability of neoplasia because intermittent bleeding from an adenoma or early cancer rarely causes anaemia. Colonoscopy also allows removal of adenomas, which is where the mortality reduction largely comes from. Surveillance intervals after the procedure are then set by the number, size and histology of anything found.
key_points: A positive screening test is a diagnostic indication for colonoscopy, not a reason to repeat the test
Roughly one in twenty to thirty positive tests reflect a cancer and about a third an advanced adenoma
Australian guidance targets colonoscopy within 30 days of the positive result
Normal haemoglobin, normal ferritin and visible haemorrhoids do not explain away the result
Computed tomography colonography is a fallback for incomplete or unsafe colonoscopy, not a triage test
explanation.pearls: Delay beyond about 120 days from a positive screening test to colonoscopy is associated with a measurably higher stage at diagnosis, which is why the 30 day target exists rather than a vague expression of urgency.

sources.label: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer

options.rationale: A repeat test cannot lower the risk conferred by the first positive result and its false negative rate would falsely reassure both of you. Repeat testing belongs to the screening interval after a negative result, not after a positive one (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer

options.rationale: Attributing a positive screening result to visible anal pathology is the commonest reason a colorectal cancer diagnosis is delayed, since haemorrhoids are present in a large share of this age group and coexist with neoplasia. Anorectal findings are only accepted as the explanation after the colon has been cleared (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer

options.rationale: About one in twenty to thirty people with a positive screening test have a cancer and a further third have advanced adenomas, so colonoscopy is the required diagnostic step regardless of symptoms or a normal haemoglobin. Australian guidance sets a target of colonoscopy within 30 days of the positive result because longer delays are associated with more advanced disease at diagnosis (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer

options.rationale: Computed tomography colonography cannot biopsy or remove a lesion, so an abnormal study simply generates the colonoscopy that should have been done first. It is reserved for patients in whom colonoscopy is incomplete or unsafe (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Clinical practice guidelines for colorectal cancer

options.rationale: Faecal calprotectin measures mucosal inflammation to help separate inflammatory bowel disease from functional symptoms in younger patients, and a normal value does not exclude a colonic neoplasm. Using it here would introduce a test that cannot change the indication for colonoscopy (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal).

explanation.summary: Duration of anticoagulation after venous thromboembolism is decided by whether the event was provoked and by bleeding risk, not by whether the clot has resolved on imaging. Events provoked by a major transient factor are treated for three months and stopped, whereas unprovoked proximal events carry a persistent recurrence risk that justifies extended therapy in patients who bleed rarely. Reduced dose apixaban or rivaroxaban after the initial treatment period retains most of the protective effect with a bleeding rate close to placebo in trial populations. Residual vein thrombus and D-dimer measured after cessation refine risk in research settings but do not replace the provoked versus unprovoked distinction. Every extended plan needs a scheduled reassessment because bleeding risk rises with age and comorbidity.
key_points: Provoked by a major transient factor means three months then stop; unprovoked usually means extended therapy
Extended therapy uses the reduced dose of apixaban or rivaroxaban after the first six months
Aspirin is markedly less effective than a reduced dose direct oral anticoagulant for this indication
Inherited thrombophilia testing rarely changes duration and is not routine
Extended means indefinite with review, not a second fixed course
explanation.pearls: Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily started after six months of treatment dose therapy cut recurrent venous thromboembolism by about 80 per cent in the AMPLIFY-EXT trial with major bleeding no higher than placebo.

sources.label: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand: Venous thromboembolism guidance

options.rationale: Three months treats the index event but leaves an unprovoked clot with a recurrence risk of roughly 10 per cent in the first year and 30 per cent by five years. Stopping is the right choice when a major transient provoking factor such as recent surgery was present (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular).

For an unprovoked proximal event in a patient with low bleeding risk, extended anticoagulation is recommended, and the reduced dose after the first six months preserves most of the reduction in recurrence with less bleeding than full treatment dosing. Extended therapy is indefinite with periodic reassessment rather than a fixed additional course (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular).
source_refs: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand: Venous thromboembolism guidance

options.rationale: Aspirin reduces recurrence by about a third whereas extended low dose apixaban reduces it by around 80 per cent, so it is a distinctly weaker option here. Aspirin is reserved for patients who decline or cannot tolerate ongoing anticoagulation (Source: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand: Venous thromboembolism guidance).
source_refs: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand: Venous thromboembolism guidance

options.rationale: Heritable thrombophilia results do not reliably alter recurrence risk enough to change the duration decision, which is already driven by the unprovoked nature of the event. Testing has a role mainly in selected antiphospholipid syndrome assessments where a positive result changes drug choice away from a direct oral agent (Source: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand: Venous thromboembolism guidance).
source_refs: Thrombosis and Haemostasis Society of Australia and New Zealand: Venous thromboembolism guidance

options.rationale: Swapping a direct oral anticoagulant for warfarin adds monitoring and interactions without benefit in a patient with normal renal function and no antiphospholipid syndrome. A defined further course also misrepresents the risk, which does not fall away at a fixed end point (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Cardiovascular).

explanation.summary: Influenza in residential aged care spreads rapidly and carries a high case fatality rate, so both treatment and outbreak control decisions are made quickly and on clinical grounds supported by rapid testing. Neuraminidase inhibitors shorten illness modestly in healthy adults but are used in high risk groups to reduce complications, hospitalisation and death, with the benefit concentrated in the first 48 hours. Treatment is still offered beyond that window to severely unwell or hospitalised patients because viral shedding continues. Facility outbreaks also trigger antiviral prophylaxis for exposed residents, isolation of cases and exclusion of symptomatic staff, all coordinated with the public health unit. Vaccination earlier in the season reduces but does not eliminate risk, particularly when circulating strains have drifted.
key_points: Age, frailty and chronic lung disease place a patient in the high risk group where antivirals are recommended
Treatment works best within 48 hours of symptom onset and should not await formal subtyping
Oseltamivir dosing is halved when the estimated glomerular filtration rate is 30 to 60 mL/min/1.73m2
Inhaled zanamivir is avoided in obstructive airways disease because of bronchospasm risk
Recent vaccination does not exclude influenza when a strain mismatch or waning immunity is possible
explanation.pearls: In a declared aged care facility outbreak, oseltamivir prophylaxis is offered to exposed residents for at least ten days and continued until seven days after the last case onset, which is a separate decision from treating the index cases.

sources.label: Communicable Diseases Network Australia: Influenza guidelines

options.rationale: She is in a high risk group by age, frailty and chronic lung disease, is within 48 hours of symptom onset, and has a laboratory confirmed infection, which is the clearest indication for a neuraminidase inhibitor. The dose is halved when the estimated glomerular filtration rate falls between 30 and 60 mL/min/1.73m2 (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Benefit is greatest within 48 hours of onset and she is inside that window, so withholding therapy discards the intervention most likely to prevent progression in a frail resident. Supportive care alone is appropriate for a well younger adult presenting late (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

A modest C reactive protein rise with no consolidation and a positive viral test does not support bacterial pneumonia, and antibacterial therapy would be added later if new focal signs or lobar consolidation emerged. This is the reflex that drives unnecessary antibiotic use in outbreak settings (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

The inhaled route risks bronchospasm and is avoided in people with obstructive airways disease, and it also demands an inspiratory effort that many frail residents cannot generate. It is an alternative where oseltamivir resistance is documented in someone without airways disease (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Subtyping does not change the choice of a neuraminidase inhibitor and waiting would push her past the 48 hour window where treatment works best. Confirmatory subtyping matters for public health surveillance rather than for this treatment decision (Source: Communicable Diseases Network Australia: Influenza guidelines).
source_refs: Communicable Diseases Network Australia: Influenza guidelines

explanation.summary: Acne severity for treatment purposes is judged by lesion type and by consequences rather than by lesion counts alone, so scarring and psychological impact move a patient up the ladder regardless of how the skin scores. Nodular disease that persists after an adequate trial of an oral tetracycline with a topical retinoid and benzoyl peroxide is the standard trigger for isotretinoin referral. Isotretinoin requires pregnancy prevention with reliable contraception and monthly pregnancy testing in people who can become pregnant, along with baseline and interval lipids and liver function. Mood should be asked about before and during treatment, though a causal link with depression has not been established. Early referral is the main lever available to prevent permanent scarring.
key_points: Assess response to an oral tetracycline at about three months rather than continuing indefinitely
Scarring, nodular disease and significant psychological impact all justify escalation to isotretinoin
Topical antibiotics are always paired with benzoyl peroxide to limit resistance
Isotretinoin in Australia is a dermatologist authority prescription with mandatory pregnancy prevention
Combined oral contraception is an adjunct for hormonal pattern acne, not a rescue for scarring nodules
explanation.pearls: Isotretinoin is teratogenic through its whole course and for one month after the last dose, so pregnancy must be avoided from one month before starting until one month after finishing, with monthly testing in between.

options.rationale: Response to an oral tetracycline is assessed at around three months and prolonged courses beyond six months add resistance risk without further benefit in nodular disease. Continuing unchanged also allows further permanent scarring to accumulate (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

Switching within the tetracycline class rarely rescues true treatment failure and minocycline carries added risks of hyperpigmentation, drug induced lupus and hypersensitivity. It is not favoured as a first or second line agent in Australian guidance (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

Hormonal therapy helps inflammatory acne with a hormonal pattern but takes three to six cycles to work and is a weaker choice when nodules are already scarring. It would be a reasonable addition in milder disease or where contraception is also wanted (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

Nodular acne that is scarring, causing psychological distress, or failing conventional oral and topical therapy is the recognised indication for isotretinoin, which in Australia is prescribed by a dermatologist under an authority listing. Referral rather than further temporising limits the number of permanent scars she accrues (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

Topical antibiotics act on superficial inflammatory lesions and cannot reach the deep nodules driving her scarring, and they should never be used without benzoyl peroxide because of resistance. This step suits mild to moderate papulopustular disease (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

explanation.summary: Haemoptysis in an older smoker is treated as lung cancer until imaging says otherwise, because a normal chest radiograph provides false reassurance in a meaningful proportion of cases. Central endobronchial tumours are the classic cause of blood streaked sputum and are precisely the lesions a plain film is worst at showing. Computed tomography of the chest defines the airway and the mediastinum and directs whether bronchoscopy or a percutaneous biopsy is the appropriate tissue step. Non malignant causes such as bronchiectasis, tuberculosis, pulmonary embolism and anticoagulant effect are also identified on the same study. Where imaging is normal and bleeding continues, bronchoscopy is still commonly performed in the higher risk age and smoking group.
key_points: A normal chest radiograph does not exclude lung cancer in a patient with haemoptysis
Persistent haemoptysis in a smoker over 40 is an indication for computed tomography of the chest
Central endobronchial lesions are the tumours most often missed on a plain film
Sputum cytology lacks the sensitivity to change management in this setting
Smoking cessation support runs alongside the diagnostic pathway rather than replacing it
explanation.pearls: Ask specifically about the volume of blood, since more than about 100 to 200 mL in 24 hours defines massive haemoptysis and changes the pathway to urgent admission with the bleeding side placed down.

sources.label: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines
RACGP: Red Book, preventive activities in general practice

options.rationale: A repeat plain film has the same blind spots as the first, particularly the hila and the central airways where an endobronchial tumour causing haemoptysis typically sits. Interval films are used for resolving consolidation, not for excluding malignancy (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines

options.rationale: There is no fever, purulent sputum or focal sign to suggest infection, so an antibiotic trial only delays diagnosis by a further fortnight. It would be defensible if he had an acute purulent illness with focal crackles (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Sputum cytology has poor sensitivity for peripheral lesions and a negative result cannot exclude a tumour, so it does not alter the need for cross sectional imaging. Its residual role is in patients unfit for any invasive procedure (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines

options.rationale: Smoking is the reason to investigate rather than a reason to observe, since it raises the pre test probability of malignancy that this presentation is designed to exclude. Cessation support belongs in the same consultation but not instead of imaging (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines

options.rationale: Haemoptysis persisting beyond a week in a smoker over 40 warrants cross sectional imaging because a normal chest radiograph misses a substantial minority of lung cancers, especially central lesions. Parallel specialist referral allows bronchoscopy to be arranged without waiting for a second general practice review (Source: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines).
source_refs: Cancer Council Australia: Lung cancer guidelines
RACGP: Red Book, preventive activities in general practice

explanation.summary: Amiodarone contains a large iodine load and is directly toxic to thyroid follicular cells, so it produces two distinct forms of thyrotoxicosis that require opposite drug treatments. The iodine induced form arises in a gland with pre-existing autonomy such as a multinodular goitre and responds to thionamides, while the destructive form occurs in a structurally normal gland and responds to corticosteroids. Colour flow Doppler is the most practical discriminator in Australian practice because radioiodine uptake scanning is uninformative after an iodine load. Mixed forms exist and are treated with both agents, and failure to respond within a couple of weeks should prompt that combination. The decision to continue or stop amiodarone is made jointly with cardiology, since its long half life means cessation changes little in the short term.
key_points: Type 1 disease occurs in an abnormal gland with preserved or increased vascularity and responds to carbimazole
Type 2 disease is destructive, shows absent vascularity in a normal gland and responds to prednisolone
Negative thyroid receptor antibodies and no goitre argue against Graves disease as the driver
The iodine load blocks radioiodine uptake for months, removing that treatment option
Amiodarone has a half life of about 50 days so cessation alone gives no rapid benefit
explanation.pearls: A brisk fall in free thyroxine within one to two weeks of starting prednisolone 30 to 40 mg daily effectively confirms the destructive type, and failure to respond in that window is the trigger to add a thionamide for mixed disease.

sources.label: Endocrine Society of Australia: Amiodarone and thyroid dysfunction

options.rationale: Thionamides block new hormone synthesis and work in the iodine induced type where the gland is overproducing, which typically shows normal or increased vascularity and often underlying nodularity. They have little effect on hormone already released from a destroyed follicular epithelium (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology).

Amiodarone has a half life of around 50 days so stopping it produces no useful change over weeks, and the cardiologist may need it continued for rhythm control. Withdrawal alone leaves an actively thyrotoxic man with atrial fibrillation untreated (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

The iodine load from amiodarone saturates the gland and suppresses radioiodine uptake for many months, so the treatment cannot be delivered effectively. Radioiodine is a definitive option for Graves disease or a toxic nodule in a patient without recent iodine exposure (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology).

Absent vascularity on Doppler with no goitre, no nodules and negative receptor antibodies points to the destructive form, in which preformed hormone leaks from damaged follicles and corticosteroids are the effective treatment. Response is often seen within one to two weeks and supports the diagnosis retrospectively (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology).
source_refs: Endocrine Society of Australia: Amiodarone and thyroid dysfunction

options.rationale: Surgery is reserved for thyrotoxicosis refractory to medical therapy or where cardiac decompensation demands immediate control, and it carries substantial risk in an unprepared thyrotoxic patient. Medical therapy has not yet been trialled here (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology).

explanation.summary: Primary aldosteronism accounts for a substantial minority of resistant hypertension and matters because unilateral disease is curable by adrenalectomy and because aldosterone excess causes cardiovascular and renal damage beyond that explained by the blood pressure. Screening uses the aldosterone to renin ratio, which is highly sensitive to the drugs a hypertensive patient is usually taking. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists and high dose diuretics cause false negatives by raising renin and must be stopped for around six weeks, while beta blockers cause false positives by suppressing it. Angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers and dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers can usually be continued if the result is interpreted with those effects in mind. Verapamil, prazosin, moxonidine and hydralazine are the agents used to hold pressure during the washout.
key_points: Spironolactone and eplerenone require about six weeks of withdrawal before the ratio is measured
Beta blockers suppress renin and produce false positive ratios
Verapamil, prazosin, moxonidine and hydralazine are the least interfering antihypertensives during washout
Correct hypokalaemia before sampling because low potassium suppresses aldosterone release
Imaging and adrenal vein sampling follow confirmed biochemistry, never precede it
explanation.pearls: A normal potassium does not argue against primary aldosteronism, since fewer than half of confirmed cases are hypokalaemic and normokalaemic disease is now the usual presentation.

sources.label: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism

options.rationale: A mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist raises renin substantially and is the classic cause of a falsely normal ratio, so a negative result taken now could not be trusted. Testing on other agents is acceptable with cautious interpretation, but not on spironolactone (Source: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism).
source_refs: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism

options.rationale: Adrenal vein sampling is a lateralisation study performed only after biochemical confirmation, and it is technically demanding and invasive. Undertaking it before a screening ratio inverts the diagnostic sequence (Source: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism).
source_refs: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism

options.rationale: Non functioning adrenal nodules are common with age and a normal appearing gland does not exclude aldosterone excess, so imaging first misleads in both directions. Imaging follows confirmed biochemistry as part of the lateralisation pathway (Source: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism).
source_refs: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism

options.rationale: Confirmatory suppression testing is only undertaken after a positive screening ratio and is subject to the same drug interference from a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. Performing it now risks a false negative and an incorrect exclusion (Source: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism).
source_refs: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism

options.rationale: Spironolactone must be withdrawn for at least six weeks before the aldosterone to renin ratio is measured, and blood pressure in the interim is held with agents that barely disturb the renin angiotensin axis such as a non dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker or an alpha blocker. Potassium is also normalised before sampling because hypokalaemia suppresses aldosterone secretion (Source: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism).
source_refs: Endocrine Society of Australia: Primary aldosteronism

explanation.summary: Post infectious immune mediated neuropathies span a spectrum from the classic ascending motor form to variants defined by cranial nerve and cerebellar type involvement, and the variant presenting with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia is strongly associated with antibodies to the GQ1b ganglioside. Campylobacter jejuni is the commonest identified antecedent infection in Australia and typically precedes onset by one to three weeks. Cerebrospinal fluid protein is often normal in patients sampled within the first week, so treatment decisions are made clinically. Immunoglobulin and plasma exchange are equally effective and are chosen on availability and comorbidity, and corticosteroids are ineffective. Monitoring is as important as treatment because roughly a fifth of patients across the spectrum need ventilation.
key_points: Ophthalmoplegia with ataxia and areflexia after a diarrhoeal illness defines the anti GQ1b variant
Normal cerebrospinal fluid protein in the first week does not exclude the diagnosis
Immunoglobulin and plasma exchange are equivalent; corticosteroids are ineffective
Serial forced vital capacity and single breath count detect impending respiratory failure
Preserved limb power does not exclude progression to generalised weakness
explanation.pearls: A forced vital capacity below about 20 mL/kg, or a fall of more than 30 per cent from baseline, is the trigger for intensive care review well before oxygen saturation or blood gases become abnormal.

sources.label: Stroke Foundation: Clinical guidelines for stroke management
Brain: Fisher syndrome and the anti GQ1b antibody spectrum

options.rationale: The triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia after a diarrhoeal illness is a variant of acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, and immunoglobulin is given without waiting for confirmatory testing when disability is progressing. Serial vital capacity and bulbar assessment are mandatory because the variant can evolve into generalised weakness with respiratory failure (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).
source_refs: Brain: Fisher syndrome and the anti GQ1b antibody spectrum

options.rationale: Cerebrospinal fluid protein is normal in a large proportion of patients in the first week and rises later, so a normal early result never excludes the diagnosis or justifies deferring therapy. Waiting a week discards the window in which immunoglobulin alters the disease course (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

Corticosteroids have been shown not to improve outcome in this group of post infectious neuropathies and may delay recovery, which distinguishes them from chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy where steroids do work (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

Ophthalmoplegia and ataxia do occur in the thiamine deficient encephalopathy, but that syndrome features confusion and arises with alcohol dependence or prolonged malnutrition, neither of which is present, and it does not abolish reflexes. Areflexia with a preceding diarrhoeal illness points to the immune neuropathy instead (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

A brainstem stroke produces crossed signs, long tract findings and usually a visible lesion on diffusion weighted imaging, and it does not cause global areflexia over four days. His normal magnetic resonance imaging and subacute course place him outside any reperfusion pathway (Source: Stroke Foundation: Clinical guidelines for stroke management).
source_refs: Stroke Foundation: Clinical guidelines for stroke management

explanation.summary: About half of patients with infective endocarditis need surgery, and the three broad indications are heart failure from valve dysfunction, uncontrolled infection such as abscess or persistent bacteraemia, and prevention of embolism from a large mobile vegetation. Heart failure is the most urgent of these and drives operation within hours to days rather than after a completed antibiotic course. Prosthetic valve involvement raises the threshold for cure with antibiotics alone and lowers the threshold for surgery. Culture negative disease is common when antibiotics have been given before sampling and is investigated with serology for Coxiella and Bartonella plus molecular testing of excised valve tissue. Early involvement of an endocarditis team improves outcomes because the decision is rarely a single specialty one.
key_points: Heart failure from acute valvular regurgitation is the leading indication for urgent surgery
Perivalvular abscess signals uncontrolled infection and is a separate surgical indication
Prosthetic valve endocarditis is far less often cured by antibiotics alone
Prior community antibiotics are the commonest reason blood cultures are sterile
Anticoagulation does not prevent embolism from vegetations and adds haemorrhagic risk
explanation.pearls: A new regurgitant murmur with pulmonary oedema in suspected endocarditis mandates a surgical conversation the same day, since operating before multiorgan failure develops is the single largest modifiable determinant of survival.

sources.label: European Society of Cardiology: Guidelines on infective endocarditis

options.rationale: Antibiotics cannot reverse mechanical valve failure and the abscess will continue to extend into the root while therapy runs. A full medical course alone suits uncomplicated native valve disease with a stable valve and no heart failure (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Deliberate antibiotic interruption to improve culture yield is only considered in a haemodynamically stable patient with an indolent illness, and here it risks rapid deterioration. Serology and molecular testing on excised tissue answer the culture negative question more safely (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Rifampicin is used against staphylococcal prosthetic material infection once bacteraemia has cleared, but adding it does nothing for the acute regurgitation flooding his lungs. Its addition is a decision for after the surgical plan is made and an organism is known (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Heart failure from severe valvular regurgitation is the strongest indication for emergency surgery in endocarditis, and perivalvular abscess in a prosthetic valve is an independent indication in its own right. Delaying for a longer antibiotic course in this setting is associated with markedly higher mortality (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).
source_refs: European Society of Cardiology: Guidelines on infective endocarditis

options.rationale: Anticoagulation does not reduce embolic risk from vegetations and increases the chance of haemorrhagic transformation if a septic embolus has already reached the brain. The measure that lowers embolic risk here is removal of the vegetation at operation (Source: European Society of Cardiology: Guidelines on infective endocarditis).
source_refs: European Society of Cardiology: Guidelines on infective endocarditis

explanation.summary: Rapid or same day antiretroviral initiation is now standard for new human immunodeficiency virus diagnoses because it improves retention in care and reduces transmission, but two central nervous system infections are recognised exceptions. In cryptococcal meningitis, starting within the first fortnight increased mortality in a randomised trial through immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome in a space that cannot expand. Tuberculous meningitis carries a similar concern and is usually managed with a delay of several weeks. Control of raised intracranial pressure with repeated therapeutic lumbar puncture is the intervention with the largest short term survival benefit in cryptococcal disease, ahead of the choice of antifungal. Once therapy does begin, maintenance fluconazole continues until the CD4 count has recovered above 100 cells per microlitre with viral suppression for at least three months.
key_points: Defer antiretroviral therapy four to six weeks in cryptococcal meningitis despite a very low CD4 count
The mechanism is immune reconstitution inflammation within a non expandable cranial compartment
Therapeutic lumbar puncture for raised opening pressure is the highest yield acute intervention
Adjunctive corticosteroids worsen outcomes in cryptococcal meningitis
Same day initiation remains the default for new diagnoses without a central nervous system opportunistic infection
explanation.pearls: Repeat therapeutic lumbar puncture whenever the opening pressure exceeds 25 cmH2O, draining to about half the opening value or until the pressure is below 20 cmH2O, because pressure control saves more lives early than any change of antifungal.

sources.label: New England Journal of Medicine: COAT trial of antiretroviral timing in cryptococcal meningitis

options.rationale: A very low CD4 count is exactly the situation in which early antiretroviral therapy during cryptococcal meningitis increased mortality in randomised trials, driven by immune reconstitution inflammatory disease in a closed cranial compartment. Same day initiation is the correct instinct for most other new diagnoses (Source: ASHM: Antiretroviral guidelines).

Two weeks still falls inside the window where excess deaths were observed, and cerebrospinal fluid sterility at the end of induction does not remove that risk. Culture conversion guides antifungal stepdown rather than the timing of antiretroviral therapy (Source: ASHM: Antiretroviral guidelines).

Withholding therapy for a year leaves him profoundly immunosuppressed and exposed to further opportunistic disease, which is a far greater hazard than the reconstitution syndrome. Maintenance antifungal treatment runs concurrently with antiretroviral therapy rather than before it (Source: ASHM: Antiretroviral guidelines).

Adjunctive corticosteroids in cryptococcal meningitis worsened outcomes and increased adverse events in a randomised trial, so they do not license early initiation. Steroids are reserved for established severe reconstitution disease with mass effect (Source: ASHM: Antiretroviral guidelines).

Deferring antiretroviral therapy for four to six weeks after starting antifungal treatment reduced mortality compared with early initiation in cryptococcal meningitis, because reconstituted inflammation inside the skull raises pressure catastrophically. This is a deliberate exception to the same day start recommended for almost every other new diagnosis (Source: ASHM: Antiretroviral guidelines).
source_refs: New England Journal of Medicine: COAT trial of antiretroviral timing in cryptococcal meningitis

explanation.summary: Stevens Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis are a single disease separated by the proportion of body surface with epidermal detachment, under 10 per cent, 10 to 30 per cent and over 30 per cent respectively. Anticonvulsants, allopurinol, sulfonamides and nevirapine account for a large share of cases, and lamotrigine risk is strongly related to the speed of dose escalation, particularly alongside valproate. Mortality is predicted by the SCORTEN score using age, malignancy, heart rate, surface area, urea, glucose and bicarbonate measured in the first 24 hours. Care is largely supportive and mirrors burns management, with meticulous fluid balance, warming, analgesia, wound care and daily ophthalmic review. Immunomodulatory options are debated and are decided in specialist units rather than in the emergency department.
key_points: Detachment of 10 to 30 per cent of body surface defines the overlap band between the two named syndromes
Ceasing the causative drug immediately is the intervention most clearly linked to survival
Mucosal involvement at multiple sites distinguishes this from staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
Daily ophthalmology review prevents symblepharon and long term visual loss
The absence of facial oedema, eosinophilia and hepatitis argues against a drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
explanation.pearls: Lamotrigine must be titrated over at least six weeks, and the starting dose is halved again when valproate is co prescribed, because valproate roughly doubles lamotrigine concentrations and rapid escalation is the dominant risk factor for this reaction.

sources.label: Australian and New Zealand Burn Association: Guidelines for severe cutaneous adverse reactions

options.rationale: Immediate withdrawal of the causative drug and transfer to a unit experienced in large area skin loss are the two interventions with the clearest survival benefit, and early ocular assessment prevents the adhesions that cause lifelong visual loss. Fluid, temperature and analgesia needs approach those of a thermal burn (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).
source_refs: Australian and New Zealand Burn Association: Guidelines for severe cutaneous adverse reactions

options.rationale: Dose reduction maintains exposure to the drug driving keratinocyte apoptosis and detachment progresses over the following days regardless of dose. Slower titration prevents this reaction at the point of initiation but has no role once it has begun (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Herpes associated erythema multiforme produces true target lesions on the extremities without widespread epidermal detachment, and the shear sign is absent. Antiviral therapy would be appropriate for recurrent herpes triggered disease, not for this drug reaction (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

The staphylococcal toxin mediated syndrome spares the mucous membranes and occurs almost entirely in young children, whereas mucosal involvement at three sites is the hallmark of this drug reaction. Prophylactic antibiotics are also avoided because they select resistant organisms in denuded skin (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Immunomodulatory therapy remains contested and none of it substitutes for stopping the drug, which must happen first and immediately. Any decision about corticosteroids, ciclosporin or immunoglobulin belongs to the receiving specialist unit (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Dermatology).

explanation.summary: Idiopathic Parkinson disease is asymmetrical at onset, usually features a rest tremor, and responds convincingly to levodopa, so a patient who fails all three of these expectations deserves diagnostic review rather than more medication. Early postural instability with falls in the first year, prominent autonomic failure with orthostatic hypotension and urinary dysfunction, and rapid progression are the classic red flags for multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy. Vertical gaze restriction points to the latter, while marked autonomic involvement and cerebellar signs point to the former. Magnetic resonance imaging supports the distinction and excludes vascular and structural mimics. The practical consequences are substantial, since prognosis, driving capacity and the management of blood pressure and bladder all differ from idiopathic disease.
key_points: Symmetry, absent rest tremor and poor levodopa response are red flags against idiopathic disease
Falls within the first year and early autonomic failure suggest an atypical parkinsonian syndrome
An adequate levodopa trial means a sufficient dose taken reliably before declaring non response
Dopamine agonists and anticholinergics both worsen the autonomic burden in these patients
Rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder supports a synucleinopathy but does not identify which one
explanation.pearls: A sustained fall of 20 mmHg systolic or 10 mmHg diastolic within three minutes of standing, without a compensatory rise in heart rate, indicates neurogenic orthostatic hypotension and is one of the strongest bedside pointers away from idiopathic Parkinson disease.

sources.label: Movement Disorder Society: Diagnostic criteria for parkinsonian disorders

options.rationale: He has already had an adequate trial at a dose where idiopathic disease reliably responds, so escalation adds orthostatic hypotension without benefit. Dose escalation is the right move when there has been partial benefit and wearing off between doses (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

Symmetrical disease without rest tremor, falls within the first year, early autonomic failure and a poor response to an adequate levodopa trial are red flags against idiopathic Parkinson disease and point to a degenerative parkinsonism with autonomic involvement. Specialist confirmation changes prognosis, driving advice and the way autonomic symptoms are managed (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).
source_refs: Movement Disorder Society: Diagnostic criteria for parkinsonian disorders

options.rationale: Dopamine agonists worsen orthostatic hypotension and carry impulse control and hallucination risk in this age group, and they will not rescue a syndrome that has not responded to levodopa. They are an option in younger patients with confirmed idiopathic disease (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Anticholinergics mainly help tremor, which he does not have, and they precipitate urinary retention and cognitive impairment in older patients. His two episodes of retention make this class particularly hazardous (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Cholinesterase inhibitors are used for established dementia in parkinsonian syndromes, and no cognitive impairment has been documented here. The night time shouting more likely reflects rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder, which is a supportive feature rather than an indication for this drug (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Neurology).

explanation.summary: Acute gout in the setting of advanced chronic kidney disease removes two of the three standard first line treatments, which is why it is a recurring examination scenario and a recurring prescribing error on the wards. Non-steroidal agents are contraindicated below an estimated glomerular filtration rate of about 30 mL/min, and colchicine accumulates at the same threshold, leaving systemic corticosteroids or an intra-articular injection as the practical choices. Loop diuretics, chronic kidney disease and heart failure all raise serum urate, so this combination of comorbidities makes recurrent attacks predictable. Urate lowering therapy is started once the attack has settled, or during an attack with anti inflammatory cover, and allopurinol is begun at a low dose and titrated to a target serum urate below 0.36 mmol/L. A serum urate measured during an acute attack can be normal or low and never excludes the diagnosis.
key_points: Avoid non-steroidal agents and colchicine when estimated glomerular filtration rate is below 30 mL/min
A short oral corticosteroid course is the practical first line in advanced kidney disease
Septic arthritis is excluded clinically here by normal temperature, intact skin and prior identical attacks
Urate lowering therapy does not treat the acute attack and needs anti inflammatory cover if started
Loop diuretics and chronic kidney disease both raise serum urate and drive recurrence
explanation.pearls: Allopurinol is started at 50 mg daily when the estimated glomerular filtration rate is below 30 mL/min and increased by 50 mg every four weeks against the serum urate, since starting at 300 mg in renal impairment is the main risk factor for allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome.

options.rationale: Non-steroidal anti inflammatory drugs are effective for this presentation but are contraindicated at an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 24 mL/min/1.73 m2, particularly alongside a diuretic and an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, where the combination readily precipitates acute kidney injury. They would be a reasonable first choice if his renal function were normal (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Rheumatology).

A short high dose oral corticosteroid course is as effective as a non-steroidal agent for acute crystal arthritis and is the preferred option when renal impairment closes off both of the alternatives, with no dose adjustment needed for the glomerular filtration rate. The absence of fever, a skin break or systemic upset, together with two prior identical self-limiting episodes in the same joint, makes empirical treatment reasonable without deferring for culture (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Rheumatology).

This is the standard Australian loading schedule but colchicine is renally cleared and the Australian Medicines Handbook advises avoiding it when creatinine clearance falls below 30 mL/min because of accumulation causing myelosuppression and neuromyopathy. It differs from the corticosteroid option chiefly in that its toxicity in this man is dose limiting rather than dose adjustable (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Urate lowering therapy does nothing for the acute inflammation and a sudden fall in serum urate can prolong or worsen the attack if started without anti inflammatory cover. It is the right drug at the wrong moment, and the starting dose would also need to be 50 mg daily at this glomerular filtration rate (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

Septic arthritis is the differential that must not be missed, but it is argued against here by the normal temperature, the intact overlying skin, the normal white cell count and two prior identical episodes that settled without antibiotics. Aspiration of the first metatarsophalangeal joint is also technically difficult and is not required before treating a typical recurrent attack (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

explanation.summary: Acute compartment syndrome develops when pressure within a closed fascial space exceeds the perfusion pressure of the capillary bed, and tibial shaft fracture is its commonest cause, with young men at highest risk because of larger muscle bulk within a fixed compartment. The diagnosis is clinical and rests on pain out of proportion with escalating analgesic requirement, a tense compartment, and pain on passive stretch of the muscles within it, with paraesthesiae in the nerve traversing the compartment appearing next. Pulselessness, pallor and paralysis are late findings that indicate the limb is already lost, so a present pulse never excludes the diagnosis and waiting for its absence is the classic error. Fasciotomy of all four compartments of the leg is the treatment and must occur within hours, since muscle necrosis begins at around four to six hours of critical ischaemia and leads to Volkmann contracture, rhabdomyolysis and renal failure. Circumferential casts and dressings are split to skin as soon as the diagnosis is suspected, and the limb is kept at heart level rather than elevated.
key_points: The diagnosis is clinical, based on disproportionate pain, a tense compartment and pain on passive stretch
A palpable pulse and warm foot are expected and never exclude the syndrome
Split casts and dressings to skin immediately and keep the limb at heart level
Pressure measurement is for the patient who cannot report pain or for equivocal cases
Muscle necrosis begins at around four to six hours of critical ischaemia
explanation.pearls: Treat a rising opioid requirement in the hours after a tibial fracture as a call to examine the compartment rather than a reason to increase the dose, since escalating analgesia need is the earliest sign and appears well before any sensory or motor change.

sources.label: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome

options.rationale: Pain out of proportion requiring escalating opioid, a tense compartment, pain on passive stretch of the compartment muscles and early sensory loss in the deep peroneal nerve distribution constitute the diagnosis, and irreversible muscle necrosis begins within four to six hours of the onset of ischaemia. Splitting the cast and all dressings to skin relieves external pressure while theatre is arranged, and the palpable pulse is expected because compartment pressure rarely exceeds systolic arterial pressure (Source: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome).
source_refs: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome

options.rationale: Elevating above the heart reduces arterial inflow and therefore the perfusion pressure across the compartment, which worsens the ischaemia, so the limb is kept at heart level while definitive treatment is arranged. Another hour of observation also falls inside the window in which muscle necrosis becomes irreversible (Source: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome).
source_refs: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome

options.rationale: Arterial imaging answers a question about large vessel flow, which is intact given a palpable pulse, a warm foot and normal capillary refill, and the problem lies within the compartment at pressures well below systolic. Waiting for a scan is the commonest reason the diagnosis is made too late (Source: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome).
source_refs: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome

options.rationale: Pressure measurement is valuable in the obtunded, intubated or regionally anaesthetised patient who cannot report pain, and in equivocal cases, but in an awake patient with clear clinical findings it delays surgery without changing the decision. A single absolute threshold is also inferior to the difference between diastolic pressure and compartment pressure (Source: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome).
source_refs: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome

options.rationale: Escalating analgesia treats the symptom that is the earliest and most reliable sign of the diagnosis, and rising opioid requirement after a fracture should trigger examination rather than more medication. Two further hours in this setting is the difference between a recoverable limb and a contracture (Source: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome).
source_refs: Australian Orthopaedic Association: Acute compartment syndrome

explanation.summary: Inflammatory back pain is defined by onset before the age of 45, insidious onset, morning stiffness beyond 30 minutes, improvement with exercise but not with rest, and night pain that wakes the patient in the second half of the night. Recognition of non radiographic axial spondyloarthritis changed practice by accepting that patients can have active sacroiliitis on MRI years before radiographic erosion appears, and that a normal radiograph therefore excludes nothing in a young patient. Extra articular features carry heavy diagnostic weight and include acute anterior uveitis, psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease, enthesitis and dactylitis, along with a family history of any of these. Normal inflammatory markers occur in roughly half of patients and are not a rule out. Treatment begins with regular non-steroidal anti inflammatory drugs and structured exercise, escalating to tumour necrosis factor or interleukin 17 inhibitors when disease activity persists.
key_points: Night pain waking the patient with morning stiffness over an hour, better with movement, defines inflammatory back pain
Normal sacroiliac radiographs do not exclude the diagnosis in a patient under 45
MRI detects bone marrow oedema years before structural erosion is visible
Inflammatory markers are normal in about half of patients
Acute anterior uveitis and a family history of psoriasis are strong supporting features
explanation.pearls: Acute anterior uveitis occurs in about a third of patients with axial spondyloarthritis and often precedes the back pain, so a young adult presenting with a first unilateral painful red eye should be asked directly about early morning back stiffness lasting more than half an hour.

options.rationale: HLA-B27 contributes to a probabilistic classification but cannot make the diagnosis on its own, since it is carried by about 8 per cent of the Australian population and is absent in roughly 10 to 20 per cent of affected patients. It supports rather than confirms, and it does not show whether inflammation is active now (Source: Australian Rheumatology Association: Axial spondyloarthritis).

Structural erosion takes years to become visible on plain films, so a normal radiograph in a young patient with eight months of symptoms indicates non radiographic disease rather than absence of disease, and MRI detects the bone marrow oedema that is present long before that. A normal C reactive protein is also expected here, since inflammatory markers are normal in around 40 to 50 per cent of cases and cannot be used to exclude the diagnosis (Source: Australian Rheumatology Association: Axial spondyloarthritis).

CT resolves cortical erosion better than plain film but shows only structural damage, which is the late finding, and it delivers substantial pelvic radiation to a young man. It differs from the preferred imaging in exactly this way: it sees the scar rather than the fire (Source: Australian Rheumatology Association: Axial spondyloarthritis).

Exercise therapy is a genuine part of long term management but deferring the diagnosis by another six months forfeits the window in which treatment limits structural progression. The average delay from symptom onset to diagnosis in this condition is already measured in years (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Rheumatology).

Discogenic pain is worse with activity and relieved by rest, whereas this man is worse on rest days and better with movement, and he has no radicular signs or positive straight leg raise. Imaging the lumbar spine also misses the sacroiliac joints, which are where the diagnostic finding lies (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Rheumatology).

explanation.summary: Clostridioides difficile infection is defined by diarrhoea plus a positive stool test, and testing should be performed only on unformed stool because colonisation without disease is common, particularly in hospital inpatients. Severity is graded on white cell count above 15 x10^9/L, a creatinine more than 1.5 times baseline, albumin below 30 g/L and evidence of colitis, and severity determines whether metronidazole is acceptable or enteral vancomycin is required. The precipitating antibiotic is stopped or narrowed wherever possible and proton pump inhibitors are reviewed. Fulminant disease with ileus, megacolon or shock requires oral or nasogastric vancomycin at a higher dose with intravenous metronidazole added and early surgical involvement. Recurrence occurs in about one in five patients after a first episode and is treated with a tapered vancomycin course, fidaxomicin or faecal microbiota transplantation.
key_points: Severity is graded on white cell count, creatinine, albumin and evidence of colitis
Intravenous vancomycin has no luminal activity and does not treat this infection
Enteral vancomycin 125 mg six hourly for ten days is first line for severe disease
Antimotility agents are avoided because of the risk of toxic megacolon
Repeat toxin testing does not assess response as the assay stays positive for weeks
explanation.pearls: Stop the precipitating antibiotic at the same time as starting treatment wherever the underlying infection allows, since continuing it roughly doubles the risk of recurrence after the ten day course finishes.

sources.label: Gastroenterological Society of Australia: Clostridioides difficile infection

options.rationale: Vancomycin given intravenously is not excreted into the colonic lumen in meaningful concentrations, so it has no activity against a pathogen confined to the bowel lumen despite being the right drug. This route distinction is the commonest prescribing error in this infection (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Metronidazole remains an option for mild disease but is inferior to oral vancomycin for severe disease, with lower cure rates and more recurrence, and this woman meets severity criteria on her white cell count and creatinine. It becomes the fallback only when oral vancomycin is unavailable (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

A white cell count above 15 x10^9/L and a creatinine rise to more than 1.5 times baseline both define severe disease, for which enteral vancomycin delivered directly to the colonic lumen is first line in Australian practice. The low dose is deliberate because the drug is not absorbed and acts topically on the mucosa (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).

Antimotility agents slow luminal clearance of toxin and have been associated with progression to toxic megacolon, so they are avoided in this infection.
